images.title: Three pencils as paper strips
images.purpose: Show lengths in cm on a bar graph: three paper strips as long as pencils of 9 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm stand on a base, with a ruler along the vertical line to read their heights.
images.composition: A graph with a small ruler along the vertical line (0 to 10, called cm), a horizontal base with Pencil 1, Pencil 2 and Pencil 3, and three amber strips of equal width.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, one graph of lengths. The label cm is centred at (240, 70) in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px). RULER: a small ruler standing along the vertical line, a white rectangle with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), x 190 to 290 and y 118 to 662, with exactly 11 tick marks on its right edge, each 30 px long running left from x 290, at y 650 for 0 and one every 52 px up to y 130 for 10 (so the marks are at y 650, 598, 546, 494, 442, 390, 338, 286, 234, 182 and 130), numbered 0 to 10 on the ruler to the left of the ticks (centred at x 225, dark #1F2937 bold, 30 px). The right edge of the ruler is the vertical line of the graph, x 290, dark #2B2B2B, 4 px, from y 662 up to y 118. BASE: a horizontal base line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at y 650 from x 290 to x 1300. BARS: exactly 3 paper strips, all 150 px wide, drawn as plain rectangles filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark outline (3 px) and a straight top edge, standing on the base: Pencil 1 strip: x 485 to 635, y 182 to 650 (height 468 px, which is 9 cm); Pencil 2 strip: x 765 to 915, y 338 to 650 (height 312 px, which is 6 cm); Pencil 3 strip: x 1045 to 1195, y 442 to 650 (height 208 px, which is 4 cm). Under the base, centred under each strip at y 700, its name in dark #1F2937 bold (36 px): Pencil 1, Pencil 2 and Pencil 3. No number is written on a strip, no total or difference is written, and no word such as Activities appears. In all there are 3 strips and 11 ruler marks. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a strip whose height differs from 9 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm, or strips of unequal width
a ruler whose marks are not equally spaced or whose numbers do not run from 0 to 10
a number written on a strip, or a difference or total written anywhere
images.takeaway: On this graph the vertical line is a ruler: the height of a strip is its length in cm, the tallest strip is the longest, and the difference of the heights is how much longer.
images.description: A graph of lengths with a ruler along the vertical line marked 0 to 10 cm and three paper strips of 9 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm standing on a base named Pencil 1, Pencil 2 and Pencil 3.
images.context: Concept image for A Bar Graph of Lengths. It follows the idea of the book's graph for paper strips (strips of equal width pasted along a horizontal line against a vertical line marked in cm) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: pencils of 9 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student read each strip's height on the ruler and then find how much longer the longest strip is than the shortest. The slip to watch: reading the length from the top of the ruler instead of from the base, where 0 is.

image_decisions.why: A graph with a ruler along the vertical line shows that the height of a strip is its length in cm.
